findings.title: Unstake could be blocked for certain users
findings.description: The vulnerability arises when a user attempts to unstake tokens from a validator that does not have sufficient staked tokens to cover the unstake amount. In such cases, the contract attempts to cover the shortfall by withdrawing from contract rewards. However, if the entire unstake amount is sourced from the contract rewards, the actual_amount_to_unstake becomes zero, which causes the undelegate message to fail due to a validation check in the Cosmos SDK that requires the amount to be positive. The root cause is the lack of a check before submitting the undelegate message when the calculated amount is zero. An attacker could potentially force a state where the last user to unstake is blocked by exhausting validator stake and relying solely on contract rewards. This would prevent certain users from unstaking their funds, leading to a partial denial of service for those users.

findings.title: Erroneous mint-fee message
findings.description: The contract unnecessarily includes a mint_treasury_fees message in both internal_stake and internal_unstake functions even when there are no rewards to distribute or when the fee amount is zero. This occurs because the contract does not check whether validator_total_rewards or the computed fee is nonzero before creating the mint message. The root cause is the absence of a conditional check around the mint_treasury_fees call. While this does not result in incorrect state or loss of funds, it leads to unnecessary transaction messages being generated, which increases gas costs and bloats transaction logs. An attacker cannot exploit this for financial gain, but repeated calls in zero-reward scenarios could lead to inefficient use of resources. The impact is limited to operational inefficiency and slightly increased costs.
